source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Interpretable and Steerable Features in VLA Models
source.authors: Aiden Swann; Lachlain McGranahan; Hugo Buurmeijer; Monroe Kennedy; Mac Schwager

page_placements.theme: Dictionary features and other non-neuron directions (SAE, NMF, PCA, codes, CAVs, optimised neuron combinations) are more interpretable or concept-selective than native neurons

record.tranche_reason: The study samples and labels interpretable activation units in VLA models, comparing SAE features with raw FFN neurons using a different method from the claim’s neuron-pole audit.
record.gate_note: The study reports interpretability sampling results for SAE features and FFN neurons. Its general-feature percentages, steering outcomes, and ablation outcomes do not measure the interpretability share named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The only result on a claim version is r8: 20 randomly sampled FFN neurons in π0.5-DROID's Gemma-2B backbone (layer PG5) were labelled for interpretability, and 6/20 were interpretable. That is a neuron-level interpretability share in a new setting (a VLA), measured by a different method: mean-pooled timestep activations and temporal-pattern labels. The SAE rows (r1–r7) measure learned dictionary features, not neurons. No version is about SAE feature shares, so those rows bear on none.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the SAE basis is substantially more interpretable than raw FFN neurons under a matched temporal pipeline (79.2% vs 30%), though some FFN neurons remain meaningful and steerable.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on VLA residual-stream activations and manually labels sampled units using temporal trajectory patterns; it compares these with FFN neurons, rather than auditing neuron poles in a language model.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported interpretability share varies by unit basis, model, dataset, and layer; the study does not isolate these as causal factors.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features in VLA residual streams are labelled interpretable at 70–90% per dictionary (95/120 overall), versus 30% for FFN neurons in one matched layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learned sparse dictionary yields a denser set of interpretable units than the native neuron basis (a counter-position to neurons already being clean).

fits_no_version.finding: Single SAE features steer object choice (+9 to +21 of 25 trials) and gripper closure far more than FFN-neuron directions selected by LM-head projection (+1 to +4; closure 0.361 vs 0.653).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are more effective steering units than native FFN neurons in VLAs.

record.code_released: not stated; project page: https://drvla.github.io (the paper says the software package is to be released)
record.problems: Interpretability is manually judged on small random samples (20 units per listed dictionary; 20 FFN neurons), with no uncertainty intervals reported. The FFN-neuron comparison is from DROID PG5, whereas the SAE aggregate spans multiple models, layers, and datasets.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or neuron-pole shares.
Only one 2B VLA backbone layer is sampled. No MoE models, no scale range, no pure language-model setting, no pole-level or one/two-job breakdown.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No test of architecture, regularization or neuron-level tool quality as causes of neuron interpretability. The SAE-vs-neuron comparison swaps the unit rather than improving neuron tools.
No test of explanations predicting held-out firing. The authors note that clean top activations do not imply steerability, but that is about causal effect, not prediction.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' label is removed. SAE shares are not neuron shares, and swapping units is not 'better tools on neurons'. If anything, the result runs against the essay's thesis that neurons are already clean. The neuron result (r8) is weak evidence for three reasons: 20 neurons from one layer; activations averaged over ~790 tokens per timestep, which may blur token-level neuron selectivity; and a robotics-behaviour labelling criterion. 281 of 16,384 neurons were inactive on the DROID subset.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole counts, or estimates of one-job, two-related-job, or not-understood shares.
No cross-scale language-model comparison, dense-versus-MoE comparison, or estimates up to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, shared-pose interpretation, or recursive-generalization analysis.

The study compares SAE features with FFN neurons in VLA models, but does not test architecture or regularization as causes, estimate InceptionV1-sized vision-model interpretability, or establish the claim’s estimated 5%–99% range.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model-native neurons suffice to explain behavior without a trained replacement model.
The study visually inspects activation patterns across episodes but does not test whether a written explanation predicts firing on examples it was not written from.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating their predicted activations on new text.

rows.subject: π0.5
rows.operation_detail: Randomly sampled FFN neurons were evaluated using the same activation-space analysis, feature search, visualization, and labeling procedure as SAE features.
rows.locator: Appendix D, Table 8 and Appendix D.1
rows.note: Two of the 14 labeled non-interpretable neurons were inactive. The paper reports that 16,103 of 16,384 FFN neurons fired at least once in the DROID subset.
rows.check: Relinked from V4 to V2. This is a neuron interpretability share in another transformer (Gemma-2B backbone inside a VLA): 30% vs the ~90% one-job share the version expects. Methodological caveats: n=20; activations are mean-pooled over all tokens per timestep; labels are based on behavioural temporal patterns; there is no pole split or one-vs-two-job split. The system is a robotics VLA, not a pure language model.

statements.correction: 6/20 (30%) of pi0.5-DROID PG5 FFN neurons were interpretable vs 95/120 (79.2%) SAE features, under the same temporal pipeline. The authors say this isolates the neuron basis vs the SAE basis. SAE per-dictionary shares are 70-90% across six dictionaries, with no causal analysis of model, dataset or layer. Limitations: per-token features were generally less interpretable than mean-pooled ones.
statements.problem: The paper does not state that the interpretability share varies with unit basis, model, dataset and layer, or that it leaves these causes unisolated. It says its matched pipeline isolates the FFN-neuron vs SAE basis difference. FFN neurons were sampled in only one model, dataset and layer.
